title: Winnipeg police shot man as only option: judge
article: A judge says Winnipeg police had no choice but to shoot a 21-year-old man who later died in hospital.
Provincial court Judge Judith Elliott says in an inquest report that if Zunga Bashir had not ignored police warnings, he would still be alive.

Police were called to a downtown apartment in December 2005 and found Bashir stabbing another man on a couch. The inquest was told Bashir was warned at least twice to drop a knife he was holding, and when he continued to stab the victim, was shot once through the abdomen.
The victim, who had been stabbed approximately 40 times, died soon after the attack and Bashir died after being brought to hospital.
The inquest report says officers had a duty to try to stop the stabbing and did what they could.
